goal: Milestone M5: build src/adapters/codex. Register the Parley MCP server at user level in ~/.codex/config.toml [mcp_servers.mcp-parley] merged with smol-toml (keep comments and every other table), write Codex lifecycle hooks to ~/.codex/hooks.json (SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/PostToolUse/Stop/SessionEnd, same roles as the Claude Code adapter, subagent payloads ignored), and an app-server idle-wake client (turn/start for an idle thread, turn/steer with expectedTurnId for a busy one) gated to the verified protocol (codex 0.154.0, v2) and fail-closed (unreachable/wrong version -> outlook 'queued until the next turn', fall back to hooks). Idempotent install, byte-for-byte uninstall, doctor that reports untrusted hooks and never falsely claims trusted. setup tells the human to trust the hooks via /hooks. Reuse the M4 patterns the live test proved: absolute launcher (never npx), MCP key mcp-parley, never overwrite/remove a foreign entry, identity bound to the harness session via PARLEY_HARNESS, monitor/drain lines carrying the message id and a reply hint, heartbeat on every poll. All tests use a temporary HOME and fake runners/sockets; never touch the real ~/.codex, never start codex sessions.
rollback_plan: Revert the M5 commits on the local branch (git revert); the only files touched are under src/adapters, src/cli, src/mcp and test, plus docs and package.json/pnpm-lock.yaml for the smol-toml add. smol-toml is on PLAN's allowed runtime-dependency list (pinned exact version). No external services, no production data, no repo writes: all install/uninstall/app-server work targets a temporary HOME and fake sockets in tests; the real ~/.codex is never read or written and no codex session is started. Nothing published or pushed.

scope_changes.reason: smol-toml is added as a runtime dependency to merge ~/.codex/config.toml while preserving comments and other tables (PLAN section 3 lists smol-toml as an allowed runtime dependency, explicitly 'smol-toml (Codex config)'; the task brief directs its use).
